subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Sustainable Engineering: Building Without Destroying
description: A 60-second lesson on Sustainable Engineering: Building Without Destroying.

hook.text: Concrete accounts for 8% of global CO2 emissions. If cement were a country, it would be the third-largest emitter.

buildup.text: Life cycle assessment evaluates environmental impact from raw material to disposal. The full picture often surprises engineers.

discovery.text: Circular engineering designs products for disassembly and reuse. Buildings become material banks — every beam tagged for reuse.

twist.text: Mass timber uses engineered wood instead of steel and concrete. Wood stores carbon. An 18-story timber tower stands in Norway.

climax.text: The next generation inherits incredible tools and existential responsibility. What they build will shape the planet's future.

punchline.text: Build it. Use it. Disassemble it. Reuse it. Engineering in circles.

quiz.question: What percentage of global CO2 emissions does concrete production account for?
options: About 2%, making it a minor contributor to climate change
About 8%, making cement the third-largest emitter if it were a country
About 25%, making it the single largest industrial source of CO2
